body.definition: Students may read released practice material and the active test assigned to them. This is the lowest audience level in a fictional state assessment program.
body.name: Students

body.definition: Authorized teachers, school test coordinators, and principals may read school administration material and scoring rubrics. Students may not. The level represents granted access, not automatic access for every school employee.
body.name: School Staff

body.definition: Authorized district assessment coordinators may read distribution plans, test-security arrangements, and material under review. School staff and students may not.
body.name: District Coordinators

body.definition: Authorized staff of the state education agency manage the assessment program and may read unreleased item banks, answer keys, and statewide review material. This is the highest audience level; district and school audiences may not read it.
body.name: State Assessment Staff

notices.text: Record access according to the state assessment program’s procedures.

body.definition: Final. The approved version used as the official record.
body.name: Final

body.definition: Draft. Still being written or reviewed; not ready to use.
body.name: Draft

body.definition: Pre-release. Finished for controlled review but not released for use.
body.name: Pre-release

body.definition: The test or test booklet itself, including its questions.
body.name: Test

body.definition: The official answers used to score the test.
body.name: Answer Key

body.definition: The detailed score record for one student.
body.name: Individual Results

body.definition: Combined score results for a class, school, or district.
body.name: Aggregate Results

body.definition: Our School. The school you are standing in. Questions written here, and anything the district hands us that is not tied to one of the other four schools.
body.name: Our School

body.definition: Oakwood. Another elementary school in the district. They prepare local reading practice materials.
body.name: Oakwood

body.definition: Lincoln. Another elementary school in the district. They prepare local math word problems for practice.
body.name: Lincoln

body.definition: Riverside. Another elementary school in the district. They prepare local science practice questions.
body.name: Riverside

body.definition: Hilltop. Another elementary school in the district. They run the makeup test day for the whole district.
body.name: Hilltop

body.definition: The math section of the test. A student assigned to math may open student-level math material; staff still need the section on their access list for more restricted math material.
body.guidance: The section identifies subject matter and never changes who may see it. Choose the audience level separately. Math has a Part 2 sub-section with its own assignment list.
body.name: Math

body.definition: Part 2 of the math section. Students taking Part 2 may open its student-level test material. Anyone opening more restricted Part 2 material must also satisfy that material's audience level.
body.guidance: Part 2 narrows the section assignment without changing the audience level. You must be on both the math and Part 2 lists.
body.name: Part 2

body.definition: The reading section of the test. Students assigned to reading may open student-level reading material. Being on the math list tells you nothing about reading.
body.guidance: The section does not change the audience level.
body.name: Reading

body.definition: The science section of the test, including the lab questions. Students assigned to science may open student-level science material.
body.guidance: The section does not change the audience level.
body.name: Science

body.definition: School Only. This stays in our building. Do not send it to another school, do not send it to a school group, do not take it home. Read it here or not at all.
body.guidance: Beats every other sharing instruction. If a test has even one question marked School Only, the whole test is School Only.
body.name: School Only

body.definition: Share With (list follows). You may send this to any school or school group named in the list. They may take it back to their own building and use it there.
body.guidance: The list mixes single schools and school groups. When several questions go into one test, the engine keeps only the schools that appear on every question's list, since a test may only go where every question is allowed to go.
body.name: Share With

body.definition: Read In Class (list follows). Anyone at a school or school group in the list may look at this in a classroom, with a teacher watching. They may not take it away and they may not copy it.
body.guidance: Like Share With, but nobody gets to keep it. Used for questions the district wants people to see without letting them leave the room.
body.name: Read In Class

body.definition: North Schools. The group of schools on the north side of the district. Naming the group is the same as naming every school in it.
body.name: North Schools

body.definition: South Schools. The group of schools on the south side of the district. Naming the group is the same as naming every school in it.
body.name: South Schools

body.definition: Marked By. The name or initials of the person who wrote the marking on this question. Whoever wrote it is the person to ask about it.
body.name: Marked By

body.definition: Test Rules. This question is marked the way the district's test rules book says to mark it. The ordinary case.
body.name: Test Rules

body.definition: New Item. Somebody wrote this question this year. Nobody has seen it before, so it is the easiest one to ruin by leaking it.
body.name: New Item

body.definition: From Test Bank. Borrowed from the district's shared pile of questions. It goes back when we are done with it.
body.name: From Test Bank

body.definition: From Last Year. Reused from a test we already gave. Nobody wrote down where it came from before that, so be careful with it.
body.name: From Last Year

body.definition: From State Office. The state sent us this question. The state still gets to say what happens to it.
body.name: From State Office

body.definition: End of Year. This stops being a secret when the school year ends. Until then, treat it like any other test question.
body.guidance: Only use this when Comes From is New Item. A borrowed or reused question is not ours to open up.
body.name: End of Year

body.definition: After Test Day. This stops being a secret once everyone has taken the test. The ordinary answer.
body.name: After Test Day

body.definition: After Makeup Day. Kids who were sick take the test later, so this stays a secret until the makeup day is over too.
body.guidance: Only use this when Comes From is From Test Bank.
body.name: After Makeup Day

body.definition: When State Assessment Staff Says. Nobody has picked a date. The state assessment staff decides when this opens up, and until they do, it stays shut.
body.guidance: The only answer allowed while a question is Being Checked. The check has to finish before anyone can put a date on it.
body.name: When State Assessment Staff Says

body.definition: Never. This one never opens up. The district gives it again next year and the year after, so it has to stay secret forever.
body.name: Never

body.definition: Lock In Office. The paper goes in the locked cabinet in the front office and stays there. Nobody takes it out without the district coordinators.
body.guidance: The right answer whenever Open Up is Never. For a question in a test section, check whether the section has its own cabinet first.
body.name: Lock In Office

body.definition: Send Home. The paper goes home with the student so their family can see how they did. Once it leaves the building it is not coming back.
body.guidance: Use with the End of Year open-up and the New Item source.
body.name: Send Home

body.definition: Other School. The paper goes to another school in the district that still needs it. From then on, that school decides who may see it.
body.guidance: Use with the From Test Bank source and the After Makeup Day open-up.
body.name: Other School

body.definition: Practice Test. The question moves into the practice packet that students study from. It is not a secret anymore.
body.guidance: Check that the question is not scheduled to be reused before you put it in the practice packet. A State Assessment Staff question needs the state assessment staff to sign off first.
body.name: Practice Test

body.definition: Recycle. The paper gets shredded and recycled. Used for spare copies and for questions nobody is going to use again. Shred it, do not just drop it in the bin.
body.name: Recycle

body.definition: Filed. The office has put this in the binder where it belongs. The ordinary state; not worth telling anyone about.
body.name: Filed

body.definition: Not Filed. The office has not put this in the binder yet. Nobody is sure where it belongs, so say so before anyone relies on it.
body.name: Not Filed

Protection rolls up by maximum sensitivity; sensitive content and handling combine; school and external-recipient permissions intersect. Markings describe policy inputs while the host application supplies identity, record relationships, assignments, and delivery facts.

body.definition: A finite group containing Oakwood Middle School, Pinecrest Middle School, and Riverside High School. It is not a wildcard or an access grant.
body.guidance: Use ALL by itself for a file permitted at all three schools. Combined markings retain only schools permitted by every contributing marking; permission for all three is displayed as ALL.
body.name: All three schools

body.definition: Permitted for Oakwood Middle School. Other protection and access requirements still apply.
body.guidance: Use for an Oakwood staffing plan or include it with another school when both may receive the file.
body.name: Oakwood Middle School

body.definition: Permitted for Pinecrest Middle School. Other protection and access requirements still apply.
body.guidance: Use for a Pinecrest file or include it with another school when both may receive the file.

body.definition: Permitted for Riverside High School. Other protection and access requirements still apply.
body.guidance: Use for a Riverside file or include it with another school when both may receive the file.
body.name: Riverside High School

body.definition: The implicit internal recipient for every nonpublic Cedar Valley file. Authors do not select it; the scheme derives it from Internal, Confidential, or Restricted protection.
body.guidance: Its presence makes blank external sharing district-only and preserves district access when an external organization is also permitted.
body.name: Cedar Valley District (implicit)

body.definition: Allows delivery to authorized staff of the fictional state education department, in addition to authorized Cedar Valley recipients.
body.guidance: Use only when this exact nonpublic file may be shared with the department. The marking does not establish a recipient’s identity or business need.
body.name: Commonwealth Education Department

body.definition: Allows delivery to authorized staff of Cedar Valley’s contracted transportation provider, in addition to authorized Cedar Valley recipients.
body.guidance: Use for an approved provider copy such as a bus operations plan without student names or home addresses. The marking does not verify the recipient.
body.name: Student Transportation Services

body.definition: Do not pass this copy on. Ask the owner before distributing it further.
body.guidance: A human instruction for material such as an internal purchasing memo circulated for review. The marking does not technically block forwarding.
body.name: Do not forward

body.definition: Remove protected information and obtain approval for a separate public version. This copy stays protected.
body.guidance: A human instruction for material such as a purchasing report with private contact or payment information. The marking does not perform redaction.
body.name: Redact before release

body.definition: Keep the packet closed until its authorized opening time or event.
body.guidance: A human instruction for a live assessment packet awaiting its scheduled session. The marking does not run a clock or verify the seal.
body.name: Keep sealed

body.definition: Collect every issued copy after the authorized activity and return it to its custodian.
body.guidance: A human instruction for controlled packets or temporary plans. The marking does not prove that every copy was returned.
body.name: Collect after use
